subject: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)
body:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)

Marissa —

As we get closer to rolling the incident taxonomy + required incident-bot fields, Support needs a tighter mapping from (incident category) -> (what we tell customers / what we ask Eng for / when we escalate).

We’re seeing the same pattern in escalations (esp. 5xx/timeouts): we lose 20–40 min while people debate “routing vs capacity vs runtime” and we don’t know what ETA language is appropriate.

Could you + the SRE folks sanity-check the category definitions and help us land customer comms guidance by category? I drafted a Support/CS playbook doc here:

Draft playbook (Google Doc):
https://docs.google.com/document/d/1vZx3mQyQk2r8wYl9pX3h7kL6eJcD0nSupportPlaybookDraft/edit

What we need from Product/SRE this week:
1) Clear, 1–2 sentence definitions for the top categories (so Support can classify during an escalation without reading the full taxonomy spec).
2) “First customer update” guidance by category (what we can safely say, what not to say) + what fields we should expect in the incident channel.
3) Escalation triggers (when Support should page SRE vs owning Eng team vs hold).

Examples driving this:
- SUP-1842: recurring 5xx/timeouts, unclear owner for initial 30 minutes.
- SUP-1910: dedicated capacity saturation — customer expects predictable ETA; we struggled to explain if it’s autoscaling vs provisioning.
- SUP-1977: streaming disconnects — debated edge/gateway vs runtime.

If helpful I can set up 30 min with you + Neha (Support) and we can walk through the “top 8” categories.

Thanks,
Dev

—
Dev Patel
Customer Support Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 10:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)

Dev — yes, this is the right push.

A few quick notes after skimming the draft:
- We should standardize the wording on “Capacity exhaustion” vs “Routing overload.” SRE’s current direction is:
  - Capacity exhaustion = not enough healthy GPU capacity in the target pool/region/tier to serve demand (incl. autoscaling not keeping up).
  - Routing overload = control plane/routing layer is shedding/queueing even though there is available capacity (or routing policy is misbehaving).
  (This matters for what we can promise on ETAs.)

- For customer comms, we should avoid saying “GPU shortage” or “kernel crash” unless confirmed. We can template to “degraded performance in <surface>” + “mitigation in progress” + next update time.

Can you tag in Neha’s preferred “customer-safe” language in the doc? Then I’ll do a pass to align with contract SLA phrasing.

Also: Ava — FYI this ties directly to the exec question of “are we consistent with updates + expectations.”

Marissa

—
Marissa Cole
Product Management, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)

+1. From Support leadership perspective, the main gap is: we don’t have consistent “what do I say in the first 15 minutes” guidance.

Two specific requests to bake into the playbook:
1) What constitutes “identified” vs “mitigating” for each category (we overuse both today).
2) When we can give an ETA vs when we should commit to a next-update timestamp only.

Dev — I’ll add customer-safe language options in the doc today.

Neha

—
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Support
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Feb 10, 2025 at 12:48 PM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)

Added a section in the doc:
- “Customer-safe first update” templates (by category)
- “What we need from Eng to update status” (e.g., impacted regions, % error, workaround)

Two open questions I need answered to finalize:

A) Streaming disconnects: do we want this under “Edge/Gateway” as the primary category even when symptoms present as mid-stream termination? (SUP-1977 is the example.) Support usually sees it as “runtime” because customers complain about generation stopping.

B) Dedicated saturation: can we cleanly separate “autoscaling policy misconfig” vs “fleet provisioning / capacity unavailable”? Customers ask “why didn’t this scale” and we need a consistent explanation without blaming.

If SRE has an “if X then category Y” cheat sheet, that would be ideal.

Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 11, 2025 at 9:11 AM PST
Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)

Re A (streaming): I think Support’s instinct is right *symptom-wise*, but we need the category to point to the right owning surface.

Proposal:
- Primary category: “Edge/Gateway - Streaming” when we see disconnects/timeouts at the gateway / load balancer / websocket layer.
- Contributing factor (optional): “Runtime - Backpressure” if runtime latency spikes are the driver.

If we do this, Support comms can say “streaming reliability degradation” without asserting root cause.

Re B (Dedicated): for v1 taxonomy, I’d keep it as a single category with a contributing factor.
- Category: “Capacity - Exhaustion (Dedicated)”
- Contributing factor: “Autoscaling lag” vs “Provisioning/fleet availability”

That gives you the message framing without adding more categories people have to choose from during a Sev.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Incident taxonomy: support playbook alignment (category definitions + comms guidance)

This is the right level of specificity.

Please make sure the playbook answers:
- When Support should expect an incident channel + IC (vs a normal escalation)
- When we proactively post a status page update (if applicable) vs 1:1 customer updates

And I’d like the “first update” templates to include a recommended next-update cadence by severity (e.g., every 30 min for Sev1).

Ava

- Category quick definitions (1–2 sentences) based on Marissa’s notes

Remaining ask: can Product/SRE confirm the exact category names we should use in the playbook (so it matches incident-bot allowed values)? If we’re locking v1 this week, we should sync strings now.

Marissa — if you can drop the canonical list into the doc (or paste from the taxonomy spec), we’ll finalize and share with the Support team for training.
